title: Clause evaluation during a run
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $rest$ a Boolean word, $Cl$ a clause over natural-number variables, $s$ a Boolean value, and $st$ a machine state. Suppose the suffix of $x$ beginning at position $st.P$ is the serialized literals of $Cl$, followed by false and then $rest$. Suppose every register of $st$ is at most $B$, $|x|\le B$, and $st.T=st.Z=st.C=st.V=0$. The machine can reach state $ce\bigl(s\lor \operatorname{eval}(Cl,\operatorname{asg}(st.K,st.S))\bigr)$ from state $cl(s)$, with all registers unchanged except that the input pointer becomes $st.P+|Cl\text{'s serialized literals}|$.

Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string and $B$ a natural number. For every suffix $rest$, clause $Cl$,
bit $s$, and machine state $st$, suppose the suffix of $x$ starting at position $st.P$
is the serialized literals of $Cl$ followed by a false bit and then $rest$. Suppose also
that each of the seven registers of $st$ is at most $B$, $|x|\le B$, and
$st.T=st.Z=st.C=st.V=0$. Then the machine reaches state
$\mathrm{ce}(s\lor\operatorname{eval}(Cl,\operatorname{asg}(st.K,st.S)))$ from state
$\mathrm{cl}(s)$, ending with the same registers except that the input pointer has
advanced by the length of the serialized literals of $Cl$. All configurations before the
end satisfy the run's validity conditions and register bound $B$.
